channel.title: Cybersecurity on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Cybersecurity on Best of AI

item.title: Claude Mythos 5.1
item.description: Claude Mythos 5.1 shares the same underlying model as Claude Fable 5.1, released the same day, but ships with the guardrails loosened for a narrow set of dual-use tasks: vulnerability discovery, red teaming, drug discovery, and biodefense screening. Anthropic isn’t putting it in the regular API lineup: access goes only to organizations vetted through its trusted-access programs, and pricing matches Fable 5.1 at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

item.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber
item.description: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is Google’s dedicated security model, released alongside the general-purpose 3.8 Flash on September 2, 2026, and gated behind the new Fairwind Program rather than sold as a standard API product. Google says it clears 70 percent-plus on internal vulnerability-discovery tests across 20 languages, scores 47.2 percent pass@1 on CWE-Bench, and delivers 2.6 times more correct patches to Chrome vulnerabilities than leading commercial models in the company’s own testing.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Cyber
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-5.6 Cyber on August 10, 2026, built on top of GPT-5.6 Sol and trained specifically to help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities faster than attackers can exploit them. It sits behind Daybreak Red, a new, more restricted tier of OpenAI’s Daybreak cyber defense program that requires separate vetting beyond the general Daybreak Blue access most approved security teams get. Compared with the base GPT-5.6 Sol model, GPT-5.6 Cyber has far fewer refusals on dual-use security requests, completing 95 percent of advanced tasks on OpenAI’s internal cybersecurity evaluation versus 1.5 percent for the general model.

item.title: GLM-5.3
item.description: Zhipu AI released GLM-5.3 on August 14, 2026, calling it the strongest open-weights coding model available, though the weights themselves are not landing until two weeks after the announcement. It shares its base architecture with GLM-5.2, so the roughly 50 percent jump in coding capability Zhipu reports comes entirely from extended post-training rather than a larger model. The company points to a security angle in particular: GLM-5.3 scored 84.5 percent on CyberGym, a benchmark for finding and validating vulnerabilities from source code, edging out Anthropic’s Claude Mythos at 83.8 percent and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol at 83.6 percent. Zhipu says internal security teams used the model to surface 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 projects.

item.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber
item.description: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber is a specialized variant Google fine-tuned for finding and fixing security vulnerabilities, released July 21, 2026 as part of the same drop that introduced Gemini 3.6 Flash and Flash-Lite. Rather than a general release, Google is running it as a limited access pilot restricted to governments and trusted partners, reflecting how sensitive vulnerability-discovery capabilities are treated differently from general-purpose coding models. Technical specs mirror the rest of the Gemini 3.5 Flash line, but pricing and broader availability have not been published since the model sits behind pilot-program approval rather than open self-serve API access.
